common_name: American Dream Coreopsis (Compact Rose-Pink Threadleaf Tickseed)

planting.note: Direct sow, or set out divisions or container plants, in spring into consistently moist, slightly acidic soil in full sun; American Dream comes fairly true from seed and can also be propagated by division of established clumps.

directions: American Dream is a compact, deeper-colored selection of the native pink coreopsis, forming a dense bushy clump of thread-like foliage rather than the looser, more sprawling habit of the wild species. From summer into fall it carries a profusion of small, clear rose-pink daisies with soft yellow centers well above the foliage. Unlike most yellow-flowered coreopsis, this species and its cultivars need steady moisture and struggle in hot, dry soils, so keep beds from drying out fully between waterings and mulch in southern gardens to protect roots from summer heat. Shear plants back lightly in midsummer to encourage a tidy rebloom and divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, or set out nursery transplants in spring, into lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Goldfink is an old German dwarf selection that stays compact and flowers the first year from seed.

directions: Goldfink is a long-cultivated dwarf form of lanceleaf coreopsis, staying under a foot tall while producing the same golden-yellow, orange-centered daisies as the full-size species from early summer into fall. Its low, tight mound makes it useful for rock gardens, border edging, and container plantings where the taller straight species would flop or need staking. Plant in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; like other lanceleaf coreopsis it is short-lived in rich, moist conditions and tends to rot over wet winters in heavy clay. Deadhead spent blooms to extend flowering and let a few seed heads mature at season's end for volunteer replacements, since plants are best refreshed every few years.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, or set out nursery transplants after frost danger passes, into well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Sunfire is an award-winning seed strain bred to flower heavily the first year.

directions: Sunfire is a bushy, clump-forming selection prized for its brilliant golden-yellow, two-inch daisies marked with a bold burgundy-red ring around the center disc, a striking two-tone effect that sets it apart from solid-yellow grandiflora cultivars. It is a recognized award-winning seed strain and branches freely to produce a long, heavy bloom season from late spring through late summer, especially if spent flowers are deadheaded regularly. Like other Coreopsis grandiflora selections it is relatively short-lived in hot, humid climates, typically performing best for two to three years before needing replacement or division. Grow in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; rich or poorly drained ground leads to floppy growth and root rot in wet winters.

common_name: Li'l Bang Red Elf Coreopsis (Compact Burgundy-Red Disease-Resistant Tickseed)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; Red Elf is a patented Li'l Bang series hybrid and does not come true from seed.

directions: Red Elf is a dwarf, densely branched member of the Li'l Bang breeding line, covering itself in dark burgundy-red flowers with bright yellow centers that take on a frosted white edge to the petals during the hottest part of the season. Bred from the same lineage as the larger Big Bang series, it reaches full size in a single growing season and holds its compact shape without staking or shearing. Grow in lean to average, well-drained soil in full sun; the Li'l Bang series is noted for strong resistance to the foliar diseases that trouble older threadleaf cultivars and rarely needs deadheading to keep blooming from early summer through fall. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring into moist, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Nana spreads slowly by rhizomes to form a dense mat and is usually grown from divisions rather than seed.

directions: Nana is a low, slowly spreading dwarf selection of eared coreopsis, named for the small paired lobes at the base of each leaf that resemble mouse ears. It stays under a foot tall, forming a dense mat of deep green foliage that is smothered in bright golden-yellow, two-inch daisies from early spring into early summer, earlier than most other tickseeds bloom. Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; it tolerates more shade and summer humidity than lanceleaf or grandiflora types and is notably resistant to Pythium root rot. Deadheading extends the bloom season into summer, and the spreading rhizomes make it a good low edging or small-scale groundcover that can be divided every few years to control its spread or start new plantings.
